inclusionaryZoning.summary: Portland requires a share of the units in a development of 10 or more to be affordable, or a fee in lieu. It does not shrink the envelope, but it shapes what is worth building in it. Confirm the current percentage and income threshold with the city's Housing & Community Development office.

disclaimer: These values drive an early-stage feasibility estimate. They are not a zoning determination, a permit, or legal advice. Only the City of Portland Planning & Urban Development Department can tell you what may actually be built on a parcel.

provenance.method: District dimensional standards in this file were transcribed by hand and have NOT been read back against the published text of Chapter 14. The machine that generated them had no network route to portlandmaine.gov, library.municode.com or the city's GIS. The statewide statutory pathways (30-A M.R.S. ss 4364, 4364-A, 4364-B, 4364-E) were read from legislature.maine.gov and are marked 'verified'.
provenance.warning: Zoning numbers in this build have not been verified against the City of Portland's published code. Portland recodified its entire land use ordinance effective December 4, 2024, so district standards may differ from what is shown. Treat every figure as a starting point to check, not an answer. See docs/RULES.md for the verification procedure.

overlays.name: Shoreland Overlay Zone
overlays.description: Land within 250 ft of Casco Bay, a great pond or a coastal wetland, or within 75 ft of a stream. State-mandated shoreland zoning applies on top of the base district: a 75-100 ft structure setback from the water, a 20 ft height ceiling in some resource-protection subdistricts, and DEP-reviewed standards for vegetation and impervious surface.

additionalSetbackFt.note: The water-body setback applies only to the shoreward side of the lot. The calculator applies it as an inward offset on every edge inside the overlay, which is deliberately conservative.

maxLotCoverageRatioCap.note: Shoreland districts cap impervious/structure coverage well below the base district.

overlays.name: Stream Protection Overlay
overlays.description: Land within 75 ft of a mapped stream. Structures must be set back from the stream channel and vegetation removal is restricted.

additionalSetbackFt.note: Applied conservatively as an inward offset on every edge inside the overlay.

overlays.name: Coastal Stability / Bluff Overlay
overlays.description: Mapped coastal bluff or unstable slope. Building here requires geotechnical review and may be prohibited near the bluff edge.

overlays.name: Historic District or Landmark
overlays.description: The parcel is in a locally designated historic district or holds a landmark structure. Height, massing, materials and demolition are decided by the Historic Preservation Board, not by the dimensional table. A conforming envelope is frequently not approvable at full height here.

overlays.name: FEMA Special Flood Hazard Area
overlays.description: The parcel is in a mapped 1%-annual-chance floodplain. The lowest floor must be elevated to or above the base flood elevation, which consumes height budget: in Portland, height is measured from average grade, so freeboard normally comes out of the habitable stories rather than being added on top.

overlays.name: Downtown Height Overlay
overlays.description: The peninsula's mapped height districts set the controlling maximum height downtown, overriding the base district figure. Where the GIS returns a numeric height for this overlay it is used directly.

overlays.name: Airport Approach / Obstruction Surface
overlays.description: The parcel is under a Portland International Jetport approach or transitional surface. FAA Part 77 notice and an obstruction evaluation may cap height well below the zoning figure.

statutePathways.name: Maine 4-unit minimum (30-A M.R.S. §4364-A)
statutePathways.description: Where residential use is allowed, a municipality must allow at least 3 dwelling units per lot, and 4 units per lot if the lot is in a designated growth area or served by public water and sewer. Portland implemented this in December 2023 by allowing up to 4 units on mainland residential lots and 3 on island lots, with no off-street parking required for those units.
conditions: Lot is in an area where residential use is allowed.
4 units (rather than 3) requires a designated growth area or public water and sewer — nearly all of mainland Portland qualifies, but confirm for the specific parcel.
Island lots are limited to 3 units.

statutePathways.name: Affordable housing density and height bonus (30-A M.R.S. §4364)
statutePathways.description: A municipality must allow an affordable housing development to exceed any municipal height restriction by no less than one story or 14 feet, must allow at least 2.5x the base dwelling-unit density where multifamily dwellings are allowed, and may not require more than 2 off-street parking spaces per 3 units.
conditions: The project must qualify as an affordable housing development under the statute.
The site must be in a designated growth area, or served by a public/district water system and a comparable sewer system.
The 2.5x density floor applies only where multifamily dwellings are already allowed.
This is a statutory floor. Portland's own bonus provisions may allow more.

statutePathways.name: Accessory dwelling units (30-A M.R.S. §4364-B)
statutePathways.description: Municipalities must allow at least one accessory dwelling unit on a lot with a single-family dwelling, subject to limited local standards.
conditions: Applies to lots with an existing or proposed single-family dwelling.
Counts toward, rather than on top of, the §4364-A unit minimums.

statutePathways.name: Housing in commercial zones (30-A M.R.S. §4364-E)
statutePathways.description: Residential units must be allowed in areas zoned for commercial use, subject to the statute's conditions.
conditions: Applies to areas zoned to allow commercial use.
Confirm how Portland has implemented the section for the specific district.
